DOCTOR VISIT LESSON · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Name Tag — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the name tag as the visit&rsquo;s introduction: the helpers read the tag, say the child&rsquo;s name kindly, and the visit starts as a friendship.

What is this?

A name tag is a sticker or paper with your child&rsquo;s name on it, so every helper in the room can greet them by name.

What does it mean?

Hearing your own name spoken warmly by a new grown-up is a small miracle for a three-year-old. The tag makes sure it happens — and the child sees exactly why.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card, paper, a marker and tape. The child draws, you write the name, teddy gets one too. Wear them to breakfast. The tag does its job before the real visit ever comes.

Why this matters

The name tag lesson is really a name-power lesson: a child who can say, spell and wear their own name brings a piece of home into the clinic.

What it teaches

Name recognition and early letters, identity pride ("that is MY name"), and reading social glue — helpers wear names too, so everyone knows everyone.

Words to learn

name tagnameletterreadwearhello

Say this to your child

“"Name tag! It helps people know your name. Look — the doctor has a tag too. Everybody reads everybody’s name, and now we are all friends."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "a name tag helps people know your name."
  2. Make one at home: the child decorates, you write the name big.
  3. Read the letters: "A… L… E… X!" Point at each one.
  4. Make one for teddy. Wear them somewhere fun — dinner, the park.
  5. At the clinic, point at the helpers&rsquo; tags: "they wear names too!"

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "name tag — it helps people know your name" sit over a nurse in scrubs handing a small tag to a child who holds a teddy bear in the other arm.

Ask your child

"What does the name tag say?" "Who else wears a name tag?" "How does the doctor know your name?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might wear the homemade tag for days, make one for every stuffed animal, or spell the name aloud to strangers at the store.

Out in the real world

Name tags are everywhere: shops, parties, library story time. Every one is a chance to practice "that is a name — it helps people say hello."

Try it together

Tag Factory: a basket of paper tags, crayons and tape. Tag everything — teddy, dog, the plant, dad. The child plays "who are you?" reading each tag aloud. Reading practice wearing a costume.

Understanding check

Ask: "Why do we wear a name tag?" (so people know your name) "What is on a tag?" (a name) "Does the doctor wear one too?" (yes — read it!)

Staying safe

A first name only on any tag that leaves the house. The privacy rule children learn here — names yes, addresses no — is worth teaching young.

This lesson pairs with the Name Tag flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Doctor Visit.
